title: Seq vs Seq: An Open Suite of Paired Encoders and Decoders
authors: Orion Weller, Kathryn Ricci, Marc Marone, Antoine Chaffin, Dawn Lawrie, Benjamin Van Durme
lab: Johns Hopkins University (CLSP) with LightOn (Antoine Chaffin)

code.title: JHU-CLSP/ettin-encoder-vs-decoder
code.note: MIT-licensed repository with links to the code, data and batch order (repo, about 20 minutes for the README and entry path); the training code itself lives in the orionw/bert24 fork of the ModernBERT codebase

takeaway: Compute-matched paired training (same data, recipe, 17M-1B) shows encoders beat decoders an order of magnitude larger on classification/retrieval and vice versa for generation, and 50B tokens of cross-objective adaptation cannot close either gap.

headline.k: the 400M encoder against the 1B decoder, same data and recipe
headline.d: the abstract's example; the biggest size ratio a native model wins at is 2.7x, not 10x

headline.k: MS MARCO dev at 400M: encoder against the decoder given 50B tokens of MNTP
headline.d: the retrieval gap the adaptation leaves; 0.1 at 1B and reversed at 17M

headline.k: the 1B decoder against the 1B encoder given CLM continued training
headline.d: the widest gap; the smallest models are within 0.6 points of each other

kb.n: 2018: the encoder lineage Ettin modernises; its page trains a toy bidirectional encoder against a left-to-right twin, the experiment this paper runs at 17M to 1B.
2020: the decoder-only shift this paper interrogates.
2025: supplies the DCLM, Dolma and Dolmino data sources and the open-artifact philosophy.
2021: rotary positions; Ettin extends context by raising the RoPE base to 160,000.
2022: training far past compute-optimal is what made decoder adaptation popular, and Ettin's 1B is still past it at 667B tokens.
2024: bidirectional attention added inside a decoder during instruction tuning; Ettin cites it as mixed training.
2019: the third architecture (encoder-decoder) that Ettin's pairs leave out; its page compares the three attention masks.
2025: another way to reuse a decoder's weights, as an encoder-decoder rather than a pure encoder.
2024: Llama 3.2 1B is the decoder baseline Ettin's 1B decoder beats (59.0 against 56.6).
2020: dense retrieval, the job where this paper says a native encoder stays the right default.

topics.n: encoder against adapted-decoder embeddings and rerankers, MTEB implications.

verdict: Believe the direction: with data, order and recipe held fixed, encoders win classification and retrieval and decoders win generation, at every size. Treat the size of the gaps as provisional (single runs, no error bars), the retrieval claim as within noise at 1B, the 1B generation gap as measured on a third of the data and a third of the adaptation budget, and the SciQ and SIQA nuance as a table mix-up.
